Case study 10 · Apollo Group · Profile Platform

Apollo Group UserProfile

Merged three unsynced profiles into one, then got students to fill it in voluntarily, which was the harder part.

Scroll the story

Role

First UX designer, then Product Manager for the profile and platform control

Timeline

~3 years

Team

Platform PMs, UX designers, engineers and business owners

85%profile usage
3legacy data sources unified
99.99976%of users fine with the privacy rollout

The short version

01

The problem

Three profiles on three sites, none in sync. Students and faculty saw more forms and a privacy risk, and they were right on both counts.

02

What I owned

The student and faculty profile end to end: framework, flows and forms, then the product vision and the adoption plan.

03

The approach

Ethnography showed working adults with no appetite for another social network. So the profile arrived during enrollment, earned extra credit and shipped with tiered privacy.

04

The result

85% profile usage and three legacy sources retired. Follow-up studies tied the support networks it created to better learning outcomes.

01 — Strategy

Strategy

Strategy

Complete Once and Use It

Goal:

A seamless user profile that would be engaging to fill out and be part of the benefit of your education

Strategy

A Place for Your Evolving Resume

Goal:

The profile was key to a coherent and seamless experience on the platform..

Strategy

No Small Challenges

Pain points and challenges:

  • 3 legacy unconnected data sources
  • No ability to show 3 roles
  • 0 incentive for users to adopt
  • 100% Real resistance to user adoption
  • Privacy features difficult for users to grasp

02 — Research

Research

Research

Foundations In Research

In looking at other institutions we saw how we stacked up to our competitors with what information they were collecting, how, and when.

After the business requirements of basic information required We moved on to the users of the profile:

Our primary methodology was surveys where we asked what information was required to perform their roles in the case of instructors but asked students what information they would like to see when getting to know their peers / classmates.

Dozens IDI were performed all across the US to create personas of the different student types but I was able to facilitate / participate in the data collection to prod further.

Research ·

Our findings indicated were clear: • A majority of users did not want to fill in multiple profiles • Users did not value the platform profile • User would not spend personal time on non essential tasks Oh.. and some VERY vocal users felt uncomfortable about sharing any details all ( sometimes even with classmates) “ I’m older: I barely have time to do my school work let alone talk to people in my class”

Research

Our path was clear: uncovering new focus

  • Privacy features were an absolute requirement
  • Policy would need to be created to “encourage” completion
  • There would be critical legal questions and company policy review

03 — Analysis

Analysis

Analysis · Incentivization

Incentivization Product features testing, processes and policy • I worked with Business / Educators to introduce it into the curriculum • I introduced scripts for enrollment consolers to promote it • We gave exceptions very vocal but few who resisted • We added features to cue (occasionally) participation

What Did It Do?
